_meta.purpose: Static conventions injected into builder prompts to prevent recurring wiring mistakes. Derived from observed builder log failures + interface patterns in mesh_memory.build_artifact.
_meta.usage: Builder reads this file at prompt-build time and injects the top-N relevant conventions into every build prompt's system preamble. Start by injecting ALL; add relevance filtering later.
_meta.maintenance: Append a new entry whenever the builder log shows a Smoke FAIL -> rescue with a reason that isn't already covered. Review quarterly for stale entries.
changelog: 1.0.0 (2026-04-20) - initial 21 entries from observed builder failures + interface patterns

1.1.0 (2026-04-27) - added 7 entries: MCP decorator, pgrep canonical path, BOM-safe tower IO, HTTP timeout, basicConfig double-handler, read-before-patch zo_mcp_server, standing goals never-empty rule

1.2.0 (2026-04-27) - added 3 entries from CEO transition day 1: directive_sql_must_match_live_schema, daemon_logging_filehandler_only, timestamps_must_be_iso_strings, probe_before_committing_to_url_pattern

conventions.observed_failure: Generated code imported and called write_service() as a Python function instead of POSTing to its HTTP endpoint. Triggered rescue on 2026-04-20 build_aidr_verdict_gate_test.
conventions.rule: write_service is an HTTP service listening on port 8772. Never import or call it as a function. Use requests.post with JSON body.
conventions.correct_example:
import requests
resp = requests.post('http://localhost:8772/write', json={'table': 'agent_outputs', 'rows': [row]}, timeout=10)
resp.raise_for_status()
conventions.incorrect_example:
from write_service import write_service  # WRONG - does not exist
write_service(table, rows)  # WRONG - not a Python function

conventions.observed_pattern: Most successful build_artifact entries expose ws_write and ws_query as local helper functions (see signal_discrimination_auditor.py, attestation_dynamic_evidence_check.py).
conventions.rule: Wrap write_service calls in local helpers named ws_write(table, rows) and ws_query(sql). This gives a consistent interface and lets the smoke test detect wiring correctness.
Every service-style module defines WRITE_SERVICE_URL = 'http://localhost:8772' near the top, alongside SERVICE_NAME, PORT (if applicable), and PID_FILE.
conventions.correct_example:
SERVICE_NAME = 'signal_discrimination_auditor'
WRITE_SERVICE_URL = 'http://localhost:8772'
PID_FILE = f'/tmp/{SERVICE_NAME}.pid'
LOG_FILE = f'/home/workspace/logs/{SERVICE_NAME}.log'

conventions.rule: Any module with a run() loop must include check_single_instance() + remove_pid_file() + signal_handler(signum, frame) pattern, and install SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers in run().
Services must send_heartbeat() once per cycle, writing a row to service_health table with {service_name, status, ts, meta}. Used by ManagerAgent for staleness detection.

Scheduled services follow a two-function shape: cycle() does one unit of work, run() is the forever loop that calls cycle() + send_heartbeat() + sleep(POLL_SECS). This matches the interface column in mesh_memory.build_artifact.
Never emit 'pip install', 'subprocess.run(["pip", ...])', or similar. The builder auto-installs imports as deps. Just write the imports; the build pipeline resolves them.
conventions.incorrect_example:
os.system('pip install reportlab')  # WRONG - builder handles deps
subprocess.run(['pip', 'install', 'fastapi'])  # WRONG

conventions.rule: Use a module-level logger configured via logging.basicConfig at file scope, not inside functions. Standard format: '%(asctime)s [%(name)s] %(levelname)s: %(message)s'. Log file path: /home/workspace/logs/{SERVICE_NAME}.log.
conventions.correct_example:
import logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s [%(name)s] %(levelname)s: %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.FileHandler(LOG_FILE),
        logging.StreamHandler()
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger(SERVICE_NAME)

conventions.rule: All DuckDB reads and writes go through write_service (ws_write / ws_query). Do NOT open a direct duckdb.connect() in generated code. Direct connections bypass governance and create lock contention.
conventions.incorrect_example:
import duckdb
conn = duckdb.connect('/home/workspace/Datasets/zo-mesh/data.duckdb')  # WRONG - use ws_query/ws_write

conventions.rule: mesh_memory.db is SQLite (at /home/workspace/Datasets/zo-mesh/mesh_memory.db), NOT DuckDB, and is accessed via direct sqlite3.connect() — NOT via write_service. It is a separate store from the DuckDB data warehouse.
conventions.correct_example:
import sqlite3
MESH_MEMORY_DB = '/home/workspace/Datasets/zo-mesh/mesh_memory.db'
conn = sqlite3.connect(MESH_MEMORY_DB)
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row

conventions.rule: FastAPI services launched by the builder are expected to run under uvicorn in daemon mode. Smoke test signature: '(Nb uvicorn-daemon)'. The module exposes app = FastAPI() at module level; entrypoint runs uvicorn.run(app, host='0.0.0.0', port=PORT).
All timestamps in writes use datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(). Never use naive local time, never use epoch seconds in user-facing outputs.
conventions.correct_example:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

conventions.rule: Writes that might re-run should use deterministic IDs (MD5 or SHA256 of the content's identifying fields) so UPSERT/INSERT OR IGNORE is safe. Learned from OTX/ecosyste.ms ingestor patterns.
conventions.correct_example:
import hashlib
id_source = f'{source}|{indicator}|{pulse_id}'
row_id = hashlib.md5(id_source.encode()).hexdigest()

conventions.rule: Never interpolate user-provided or external data into SQL via f-strings or % formatting. Always use parameterized queries. Threat feeds and external APIs may contain adversarial payloads.
conventions.incorrect_example: cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM indicators WHERE value = '{hostname}'")  # SQL INJECTION
conventions.correct_example: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM indicators WHERE value = ?', (hostname,))

conventions.rule: Smoke-testable modules must exit with code 0 on success. A script with a run() loop that never returns is FINE - the smoke test detects the uvicorn-daemon or looping pattern. But a one-shot script must explicitly sys.exit(0) on success.

API keys, tokens, and credentials are read from os.environ ONLY. Never hardcode. Never log the value. Common ZoComputer secrets: Alpacasecret, RH_USERNAME, PWD_ROBINHOOD_TRADING_INVESTING, Alienvaultapi.
conventions.correct_example:
import os
API_KEY = os.environ.get('Alienvaultapi')
if not API_KEY:
    logger.error('Alienvaultapi env var not set')
    sys.exit(1)
# NEVER: logger.info(f'Key: {API_KEY}')

conventions.rule: Robinhood Investing account (acct #886614932, label 'Individual') is READ-ONLY FOREVER. No generated code may place trades, modify positions, or send orders to this account. Only the trading account (zocomptrady, acct #889310942) may receive trading instructions. Enforce at multiple layers.
conventions.correct_example:
INVESTING_ACCT = '886614932'
TRADING_ACCT = '889310942'

def place_order(acct: str, ...):
    if acct == INVESTING_ACCT:
        raise ValueError('INVESTING account is read-only; trades forbidden')
    assert acct == TRADING_ACCT, f'Unknown account {acct}'
    ...

conventions.rule: Agents operating in one domain context (trading, deputyship, linkedin, sentinel) must never reference entities, names, or terms from another domain in their outputs. Historical failure: 'Christine' from deputyship agent leaked into trading output. Scope boundary is enforced by anti_entropy_agent; violations flag corrections.

ZOMesh/Sentinel work stays within the MCP trust-intelligence domain. Never reference or integrate law-firm operational risk register, firm infrastructure, client matters, or work-Robin operational security concerns. Cross-reference targets for threat intel are always Sentinel-internal tables (mcp_server_registry, mcp_registry_facts), never the firm.

When debugging a Smoke FAIL, check in this order: (1) syntax via ast.parse, (2) imports resolve, (3) required constants defined (SERVICE_NAME, PORT, WRITE_SERVICE_URL), (4) wiring (write_service called correctly), (5) actual logic. Most failures are in layers 1-4, not 5.

Each build_artifact produces one .py file at /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/{task_name}.py. Multi-file modules are not supported by the current builder smoke pipeline. If multi-file is required, chain multiple build directives.

conventions.observed_failure: Wrong decorator (@app.tool() instead of @mcp.tool()) raises NameError at decoration time and silently drops the tool from registration. The tool just disappears from the server's tool list at runtime.
conventions.rule: In zo_mcp_server.py, the FastMCP instance variable is named `mcp`. ALL tool decorators MUST be @mcp.tool(). Never @app.tool() or @server.tool().
conventions.incorrect_example:
@app.tool()  # WRONG - app is not defined; raises NameError
@server.tool()  # WRONG - server is not the instance name

conventions.rule: Before writing any patch to zo_mcp_server.py, ALWAYS read the current state via zo_read_file. Do not patch from memory. Stale NameError lines in zo_agent_health recent_errors are aging log history -- they will age out naturally; do NOT wipe logs to clear them.
conventions.observed_pattern: Recurring failure mode: patching from outdated mental model leads to overwriting legitimate recent additions. Read-first is non-negotiable.

conventions.rule: Every requests.* call MUST pass an explicit timeout argument. No bare requests.post / requests.get without timeout. Bare requests defaults to no timeout, and a wedged WriteService cascades into every daemon hanging forever.
conventions.correct_example:
requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=8)
requests.get(url, timeout=10)
conventions.incorrect_example: requests.post(url, json=payload)  # no timeout = potentially infinite hang

conventions.rule: Call logging.basicConfig(...) ONCE per process, in the entry-point script only. Library/imported modules use logging.getLogger(__name__) without basicConfig. If two modules each call basicConfig and both run in the same process, every log line prints twice.
conventions.observed_failure: Builder log shows every line duplicated as of 2026-04-27. Caused by basicConfig being invoked from both the main module and an imported helper.
conventions.correct_example:
# library.py
import logging
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)  # no basicConfig

# entry_point.py
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='...')
log = logging.getLogger('main')

conventions.observed_failure: pgrep -f 'probe_consumer' matched the launcher script /home/workspace/logs/_start_probe_consumer.py and produced a false 'already running' positive (2026-04-26).
conventions.rule: When checking if a service is alive via pgrep -f, match the CANONICAL install path (e.g. '/zo_mesh/probe_consumer.py'), not just the basename. Explicitly exclude /home/workspace/logs/ launcher scripts that may have the daemon name in their command line.
conventions.correct_example:
pgrep -f '/zo_mesh/probe_consumer.py' | xargs -r ps -p > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo running || echo dead
# Or in Python: filter out cmdlines containing /home/workspace/logs/
conventions.incorrect_example: pgrep -f probe_consumer  # matches launcher scripts that *invoke* probe_consumer

conventions.observed_failure: PowerShell 5.1 'Set-Content -Encoding UTF8' writes a UTF-8 BOM by default. Python's json.loads then rejects with 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM' (2026-04-26).
conventions.rule: For tower↔ZoComputer JSON artifacts via Syncthing: TOWER side (PowerShell) must write with [IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false)) to avoid the BOM. ZO side (Python) must read with encoding='utf-8-sig' to tolerate either case.
conventions.correct_example:
# ZO consumer:
import json
with open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Tower producer (PowerShell):
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
conventions.incorrect_example:
# ZO consumer (will fail on BOM-prefixed files):
with open(path) as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Tower producer (will write BOM):
Set-Content -Path $path -Value $json -Encoding UTF8

conventions.rule: The builder directive queue must NEVER be empty. sentinel_directive_generator.py has a standing_goals_fallback that emits perpetual goals from /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/standing_goals.json when LLM-suggested directives all dedupe. Adding new long-running daemons should add new entries to standing_goals.json so the fallback library grows over time.
conventions.observed_pattern: Pre-2026-04-27, builder logged 'No pending directives' for 90+ minutes between dirgen cycles. Robin's hard rule from the CEO transition: directives never empty. Standing goals close the gap structurally.

conventions.observed_failure: On 2026-04-27, three standing-goal daemons were generated based on directive descriptions that named columns the live tables don't have. registry_promoter v1 named columns on mcp_registry_facts that don't exist. decision_emitter named verdict/score/decided_at fields on mcp_decisions (real columns: submission_id, analyst_name, decision, conditions, expires_at). fingerprint_runner named tool_count/prompt_count/resource_count on mcp_fingerprints (real columns: tool_name_hash, description_tokens, permission_scope_hash, domain_fingerprint, version_string). Every cycle returned 400 Bad Request; daemons were idempotent so no harm done, but they did zero useful work for two hours.
conventions.canonical_mechanism: zo_sentinel/schemas/loader.py exposes load_duckdb_schema() and load_mesh_memory_schema(); probe / evaluator code calls schema.column_names(table) and schema.validate_row(table, row) instead of hardcoding columns. Snapshots live at schemas/*.json, regenerated tower-side via refresh_schema_doc.py.
conventions.rule: Directive descriptions that reference SQL tables MUST verify the column list against information_schema.columns at directive-emit time. Either: (a) include the verified column list verbatim in the description so MiniMax sees the schema as ground truth, OR (b) instruct the daemon to introspect via 'SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = X' on startup and adapt its SQL to the live shape, OR (c) consume the committed snapshot via zo_sentinel.schemas.loader (preferred for new code). Option (a) is preferred for stable schemas in legacy code; (b) for tables under active migration; (c) is the canonical mechanism going forward. NEVER let a directive author (human or LLM) name columns from memory.
conventions.correct_example:
# In the directive description, include the verified schema:
# 'mcp_fingerprints columns are exactly: server_id, tool_name_hash, description_tokens, permission_scope_hash, domain_fingerprint, version_string, computed_at. Do NOT use tool_count or prompt_count -- those are not in the schema.'
conventions.why: MiniMax faithfully implements whatever the directive says. If the directive hallucinates columns, the generated code hallucinates columns. The cost is a wasted build cycle plus a daemon that pollutes service_health with idempotent-but-useless heartbeats. Schema verification at the directive layer prevents this entire failure class.

conventions.observed_failure: On 2026-04-27, registry_promoter_daemon v1 logged every line twice. Cause: logging.basicConfig used handlers=[FileHandler, StreamHandler]. The daemon was launched with nohup which redirects stdout/stderr to the same FileHandler target. StreamHandler then wrote to stdout, which nohup wrote to the same file, doubling every line.
conventions.rule: Daemons launched via nohup-style detached spawn (the standard pattern in /home/workspace/logs/_relaunch_*.py) must use ONLY a FileHandler. Adding a StreamHandler doubles every line because nohup redirects stdout to the same log path.
conventions.correct_example: logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(name)s] %(message)s', handlers=[logging.FileHandler(LOG_FILE)])

conventions.observed_failure: On 2026-04-27, candidate_promoter_daemon v1 sent {'last_heartbeat': time.time()} every 30s for 6+ hours. WriteService logged 'Conversion Error: Unimplemented type for cast (DOUBLE -> TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE)' on every heartbeat. The daemon's main writes (first_seen / last_seen on mcp_server_registry rows) had the same bug. Combined with concurrent fingerprint_v3 load, this contributed to a WS wedge at 18:13.
conventions.rule: Any column typed TIMESTAMPTZ in DuckDB (service_health.last_heartbeat, mcp_server_registry.first_seen / last_seen / last_assessed / last_scanned, mcp_attestations.attested_at, mcp_signal_scores.computed_at, etc.) MUST be written as an ISO 8601 string. Never write time.time() (that's a DOUBLE epoch float). Use datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().

conventions.observed_failure: On 2026-04-27, candidate_promoter v1 was built on the assumption that the official MCP registry has a per-server detail endpoint at /v0/servers/{name}. It doesn't — every variant returned 404 with structured application/problem+json. The probe (_probe_mcp_registry_url.py, ~30s to write and run) revealed this in 30 seconds; the daemon had been running broken for hours.
conventions.rule: When a directive depends on an external API shape (URL pattern, response field names, pagination style), write a small probe script first that tries the candidate patterns against a known real input and reports which return 200 with the expected fields. Probe ~30s. Only commit to a URL pattern after the probe confirms it.
conventions.correct_example:
# Before building candidate_promoter, run a probe:
# - V1 raw slash: /v0/servers/ai.aarna/atars-mcp
# - V2 percent-encoded: /v0/servers/ai.aarna%2Fatars-mcp
# - V3 query param: /v0/servers?name=ai.aarna/atars-mcp
# - V5 LIST endpoint: /v0/servers?limit=1
# Report status code + first 600 bytes of body for each. Pick the one that returns 200 with the data shape you need.
